body.rationale: Voting as equal_weight (heuristic family) under a draft IPS (config/ips.yaml). I am not scored on my own ranking, so I judged which portfolios the CIO can build from. Only the return-optimized candidates and cvar_minimization pass every hard IPS limit including backtest drawdown. The exceptions are pc_researcher, which breaches volatility and tracking error but only mildly, and my own 1/N, which breaches drawdown. First: resampled_efficient_frontier. It is the most diversified compliant portfolio (effective N 13.3, no position above about 14.5%), its Sharpe is 0.41, and it has the lowest estimation-error concentration of the optimizers. Its reviews flagged thin drawdown headroom (-24.3% vs -25%) and a gamma-description inconsistency, but neither is fatal. Second: black_litterman. It is compliant with a clean execution check (effective N 6.1 reconciles), and its backtest Sharpe is 0.70. The reviewer's technical point on the Omega mechanism is a description issue, not a numerical error. Its -21.2% drawdown gives more headroom than the others in the group. Third: pc_researcher. It has the best ex-ante Sharpe among the plausible candidates (0.51), a 0.70 backtest Sharpe, a -10.9% drawdown, and effective N of 7.2. It is a different family and keeps the ensemble spanning families. The reviews showed that the delivered portfolio contradicts the rationale (near-cash, vol 3.82%), and that the Sharpe is unexplained against the floor. Those are real weaknesses, so it ranks below the two compliant optimizers. Fourth: max_sharpe. It is compliant with a 0.46 Sharpe, but 46% in us_value is a single judged CMA gap showing through, and the -24.7% drawdown leaves little room. Fifth: cvar_minimization. It is compliant, has a strong 0.74 backtest Sharpe, and a -18.7% drawdown. It carries a fitted-to-few-crises tail risk and was tuned to the volatility edge (backtest vol 7.91%). It adds a non-traditional family view. It beats volatility targeting, market-cap weighting and the near-cash risk-structured portfolios, which breach three hard limits each, and it is also more diversified than they are. First beats fifth because resampled_efficient_frontier is far more diversified (13.3 vs 2.9 effective assets) and less dependent on a tail-scenario fit, while cvar_minimization concentrates on a few hedge assets. The bottom flag goes to hierarchical_risk_parity. About 92% of the portfolio is cash, effective N is 1.4, and it breaches return, volatility and tracking error together. The reviews identify the inclusion of cash as a design choice, plus a mischaracterisation of the recursion as risk budgeting. The CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier because its orthogonality is useful in an ensemble.
